raw_comment: On the graph, something that stands out is that most of the U.S. is graphed to have a widespread drought rated as "abnormally dry," while certain areas, for example in Montana, Texas, Ohio and West Virginia have areas with extreme to exceptional droughts. The article says that droughts can be caused by many different factors, such as how much precipitation there is in an area, streamflow, reservoir levels, temperature and evaporation, soil moisture, and the health of vegetations. It can be inferred that these areas most likely suffer from one or more of these factors, causing extreme drought conditions.
